name: Notcurses
tagline: C TUI library for maximal terminals: pixels, video, planes, threads

other.label: Hacking the Planet with Notcurses (book PDF)

license.notes: COPYRIGHT file is Apache-2.0; GitHub API reports NOASSERTION because of the file layout.

language: C (C++ wrappers; Python and Rust bindings)

adoption.downloads: Distributed mainly via distro packages (Repology); Rust libnotcurses-sys 169k all-time, 954 in the last 90 days (crates.io)
adoption.summary: Respected and widely packaged, but no prominent applications found; best known for notcurses-demo and the author's own tools (ncls, ncplayer).

maintainability.recent_activity: 0 commits and 0 merged PRs since 2026-07-11; 33 commits in the past year, last 2026-05-18 (GitHub API); 332 open issues
maintainability.bus_factor: low: Nick Black has ~7,950 of the commits
maintainability.summary: Feature-complete and stable at 3.x but in maintenance mode with a single author.

architecture.summary: Notcurses abandons the X/Open Curses API: drawing happens on z-ordered ncplanes grouped into piles; notcurses_render composites planes (with transparency, blending) into a frame and rasterizes only the damage to the terminal. Cells are grapheme-cluster based with 24-bit color quantized as needed. ncvisuals load images/video (FFmpeg or OpenImageIO) and blit via the best available method — Sixel, Kitty, Linux framebuffer, or Unicode half/quadrant/sextant/octant/braille blitters. Thread safety was a design goal. Higher-level widgets (menus, readers, plots, reels, trees, selectors) are built in.
key_points: z-ordered planes and piles with alpha/blending
Pixel blitting via Sixel, Kitty, fbcon; Unicode blitters down to octants
Thread-safe C API; Python and Rust bindings
Assumes the most capable terminal and steps down
Can read back rendered cells (ncplane_contents, notcurses_at_yx)

claims.text: notcurses-demo benchmark per terminal (old builds): kitty 0.15.0 682.3 FPS / 72.9 s, alacritty 0.4.1 553.7 FPS / 74.0 s, VTE 205.9 FPS, xterm 11.87 FPS

performance.summary: The only project in this group with a published, reproducible frame-rate methodology (notcurses-demo, three runs per terminal), though the table is from ~2019-2020 terminal versions.

agent_usability.how: Code generation (C/Python/Rust). No protocol or socket.
agent_usability.integration_effort: High: C API, manual memory, app must add its own control layer.
agent_usability.readback: In-process the app can read rendered cells (notcurses_at_yx, ncplane_contents); otherwise screen scraping.
agent_usability.summary: A powerful renderer with no agent story.

score_notes.readback: Cell readback exists but only in-process
score_notes.pixel_graphics: Sixel/Kitty/fbcon bitmaps, video, plane compositing with alpha: the richest pixel story in the group
score_notes.maturity: Stable 3.x, widely packaged, few visible production users, slowing maintenance

steelman: Notcurses is the most ambitious terminal graphics engine ever shipped: z-ordered planes with transparency composited into each frame, images and full video blitted through Sixel, Kitty or the Linux framebuffer, and a ladder of Unicode blitters (half-blocks to octants and braille) when pixels are unavailable — all thread-safe, all with 24-bit colour quantized per terminal, and measured with a published per-terminal benchmark methodology. It 'assumes the maximum and steps down', which is exactly the right stance for an agent-era terminal that wants pixels. It has a free guidebook, Python and Rust bindings, and is widely packaged across distributions (Repology).
weaknesses: Single author; no release since 2025-10-28 and no commits since 2026-05-18
C API with manual lifetimes; heavy optional multimedia deps (FFmpeg/OIIO)
No widget-level declarative model or agent surface
Performance table measured on 2019-2020 terminal versions

relation_to_scene.overlap: Pixel layer under/over text, capability probing with cell fallbacks, compositing of layers.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Plane compositing with alpha and the pixel-protocol ladder with Unicode blitter fallbacks — Notcurses solved these years ago (in C).
borrow: The blitter ladder (pixel → octant/sextant/quadrant/half-block/braille) as scene's pixel fallback
'Assume the maximum and step down' only on positive terminal confirmation (it won't use bitmaps unless the terminal says so)
Planes/piles as a mental model for scene's callout and card layers
relation_to_scene.gap_left: Serializable UI, live agent control and readback, streams, hot-swap, time travel, modern maintenance.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: Its graphics engineering is the reference for scene's pixel layer, but it's a C library in maintenance mode with no agent model.
